summary: Toast stack collects the notifications an agent sends while it works and piles them into a small deck, newest in front. Hover the deck and it fans out into a list so a person can read each one and close the ones they are done with.
use: When an agent finishes several things in a row, like tests passing, a PR opening and frames syncing.
When notifications should stay on screen until someone reads them, without covering the page.
When you want a quiet corner of the app that shows the last few events at a glance.
When each event needs its own icon colour so people can tell good news from warnings.
features: Pass `toasts` oldest first. The last item sits at the front and older ones step back, shrink and fade.
Hovering the stack fans it into a list that grows to fit the four front toasts. Set `expanded` to fan it yourself.
Each toast has an icon badge, a bold `title`, an optional `detail` line and an optional `time` like "now" or "2m".
`tone` colours the badge, with status tones (ok, warn, bad, merge) and colour names like blue, purple and teal.
The close button calls `onDismiss` with the toast id. Remove it from `toasts` and it slides off to the right as it fades.
`max` caps how many toasts stay mounted (6 by default). Older ones drop off the back, and new ones rise in from below.
a11y: The stack is an `aria-live="polite"` region, so screen readers announce new toasts.
Each close button is a real button with `aria-label="Dismiss"` and a Dismiss tooltip.
A toast that is sliding away is marked `inert`, so it cannot be focused or clicked during its exit.
Under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, the shared stylesheet cuts animations and transitions to almost nothing.

faq.q: How do I add a new notification?
faq.a: Append an object with a unique `id`, an `icon` and a `title` to the end of your `toasts` array. It rises in from below and becomes the front card.

faq.q: Does the stack remove a toast when I press its close button?
faq.a: No. The button only calls `onDismiss(id)`. Filter that toast out of `toasts` in your state and the component animates it away.

faq.q: Can I keep the stack fanned out all the time?
faq.a: Yes. Pass `expanded={true}` to keep it open, or `expanded={false}` to keep it stacked. Leave it out and it fans while the pointer is over it.

faq.q: What happens when more toasts arrive than fit?
faq.a: Only the newest `max` toasts stay mounted, six by default. In the stacked view only the front three are visible, and the fanned list shows the front four.
